SATOM 2.2.0

SATOM now keeps a versioned API library for every product, and firmware answers, pre-flights and the API explorer are based on it.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
On this page
  • In short
  • What's new
  • A versioned API library for every product
  • The API versions page covers every product
  • API field renames
  • The API explorer knows the firmware build
  • The clone dialog offers the destination's new fields
  • Harvests happen on their own
  • What changes for you
  • Fixed
  • Learn more

Released: 2026-09-26 · All releases

In short#

This release introduces the API library: a permanent record of which API endpoints and fields each firmware build of each product serves, with every fact traced back to where it came from. The firmware matrix, the clone and upgrade pre-flights, the API versions page and the API explorer now all rely on it. Anyone who clones configuration between appliances, plans firmware upgrades or uses the API explorer will notice more precise answers.

What's new#

A versioned API library for every product#

  • The library is stored in SATOM's database and is never rewritten: each piece of evidence is stored once, and seeing the same content again only confirms it.
  • Facts are kept per field, per firmware build and per source, so the library grows with the number of builds, not with the number of sweeps.
  • Five products are covered:
  • FortiWeb — from sweeps and field definitions read from appliances;
  • FortiADC — from sweeps and the earlier firmware matrix;
  • FortiAuthenticator — from its own API description, read live and read-only (58 resources and 316 fields on 8.0.3);
  • FortiAnalyzer — from the vendor's published automation collection: 202 endpoints and 2,275 fields across 56 builds (6.2.1 to 7.6.4);
  • FortiGate — from the vendor's published automation collection: 723 endpoints and 11,049 fields across 37 builds (6.0.0 to 8.0.0). FortiGate is reference only: SATOM does not manage it.
  • Vendor data is labelled as vendor documentation and never outranks a measurement of a real appliance. A vendor range that is open-ended stops at the newest build the vendor data knows about.
  • New administrator commands fill the library from archived snapshots, import vendor data, ingest a file, harvest a FortiAuthenticator and show the library's status. All are safe to run again. To refresh vendor data, download the vendor collection and import it.

The API versions page covers every product#

  • A product selector now reaches FortiAuthenticator, FortiAnalyzer and FortiGate.
  • The new Library comparison compares any two builds: endpoints and fields added, removed, changed in type or renamed, with unknowns kept separate.
  • The new Endpoint drill-down lists the fields of an endpoint on a build and tells you since which build any field has existed.

API field renames#

A new page lets operators with registry editing rights record that a firmware renamed a field. Comparisons and pre-flights then report a rename instead of one field lost and another added. Mappings are retired, never deleted.

The API explorer knows the firmware build#

  • It identifies the selected appliance's exact build and shows it, with its evidence, in a banner.
  • Every endpoint in the menu is marked served, absent or unknown for that build.
  • It lists the fields the endpoint serves on that build.
  • For a build nobody has measured yet, it offers Harvest this appliance now.

The clone dialog offers the destination's new fields#

When you clone to an appliance on a newer build, fields that the destination serves and the source lacks are listed with their type, options and evidence. Nothing is added unless you fill in a value, and every value is checked again on the server.

Harvests happen on their own#

  • Every rediscovery files its snapshot in the library.
  • When the firmware check sees that an appliance changed build, it queues one background harvest. This is on by default and can be turned off.
  • A new scheduled action harvests every appliance whose build has no evidence yet. It is available but not scheduled by default.

What changes for you#

  • The firmware matrix, the clone and upgrade pre-flights and the API versions page now read the library. Rebuild still writes an export file so that the command-line version and pre-flight reports keep working when the database is down; the console itself no longer reads it.
  • The clone and upgrade pre-flights look up both appliances' exact builds and say what kind of evidence each answer is based on. If only the vendor's documentation says an endpoint is missing, you get a warning; only an appliance that actually rejected the endpoint blocks the operation.
  • The API explorer refuses to send a request to an endpoint that the appliance's build is known not to serve, unless you confirm. Overriding is recorded in the audit log. A request to an endpoint nobody has measured is sent with a warning.

Fixed#

  • Deleting or retiring an appliance deleted the evidence for its firmware build. It no longer does. One build measured only on appliances since retired had disappeared this way; it was restored from archived snapshots.
  • A rediscovery run as a job could write into the wrong database. It now always writes to the database of the SATOM instance running it.
  • A rediscovery after a firmware check replaced the appliance's full firmware string, including its build number, with the bare version. It no longer does.
